rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-six builder trees go (a row of torrey pines, corals and queen palms every 6 m along the back fences, palms 3.3 m from the house fronts, magnolias and jacarandas by the seating); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two or three houses: by the picnic table, the grill, the adirondack chairs, the beach umbrella, and on the open lot corner.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m east, 12 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the open lot corner, 23 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the back yard with the kettle grill (1.9 m off): a magnolia over the cook
the east yard with the two white adirondack chairs: shade for them
the west yard by the closed beach umbrella: a jacaranda over the lounging spot
